background.text: Secretary [target], thank you so much for taking the time to speak with Scripps News on such an important day. Let's start, of course, with this big announcement. Tell me about these 15 drugs that have been selected for drug negotiations and what savings might mean for Part D recipients.

background.speaker: [target]
background.text: Thanks for watching.

background.speaker: [target]
background.text: Jacob, this is the second year of implementation of the President's signature lower-cost prescription drug law, where we get to, for the first time in history, negotiate lower drug prices within the Medicare program. We proved it works last year when we took the 10 most expensive drugs. By the way, of the thousands, about 8,000 drugs that Medicare covers, we took just the top 10, and just those top 10 drugs cost about $50 billion or more a year for the Medicare beneficiaries who need them. And so that's not the whole population of Medicare, just those who need those drugs. That's how expensive these are, those 10. We were able to lower the list price of those drugs through our negotiations from 40% to 80% over the list price. That meant a savings of billions of dollars out of the pockets of so many Americans. Medicare beneficiaries and taxpayers. Round two started now. This announcement of 15 new drugs adds to the 10 from last year. And so together, those 25 drugs, just those 25 out of the thousands of drugs in Medicare constitute about a third of all the spending by Medicare on drugs. And so we negotiate good prices for these next 15. We're in good shape for the American people and for Medicare beneficiaries.

background.speaker: SPEAKER_01
background.text: This announcement is coming less than a week before the new administration takes over on January 20th. Are you confident that the President-elect and his team will continue these negotiations after you leave office?

ground_truth: I'm absolutely confident that using our roadmap, anyone coming into this administration can have success because it's simply a matter of negotiating. We see the facts. We see the prices. We see how much we're paying. There's a lot of running space in between to lower prices. So am I confident that we can have success as we proved last year? Well, we proved it last year. And round two, we've announced the drugs. It will be left to the next administration to do the negotiations. But there's a clear roadmap for success for the American people and for Medicare beneficiaries. And I guarantee you, Medicare beneficiaries want to see us lower the prices that they're paying for their medications.
